neighbours.label: the subject (pronoun plus its auxiliary) of a statement that someone is told or knows, directly after know/tell + person with no 'that' (knows you are there, told him she had, tell her I am); not 'why/that they should'
fire: Hold her hand so your daughter knows you are nearby.
The meeting ended when the director told them he had already signed the deal.
Could you tell the receptionist I am running a little late.
Send a short note so the team knows we are still interested.
My brother phoned and told me he was moving to Leeds.
Wave from the gate so the driver knows you are waiting.
Go and tell your grandmother we are leaving in ten minutes.
The nurse smiled and told her she was doing very well.
quiet: Hold her hand until your daughter falls asleep nearby.
The meeting ended when the director signed the deal and left.
Could you ask the receptionist why I should fill in this form.
Send a short note explaining why they should still be interested.
My brother phoned before he moved to Leeds.
Wave from the gate while you are waiting for the driver.
Your grandmother insisted that we should leave in ten minutes.
The nurse smiled because she was doing very well.

notes: Card: 'told him [she]'d been', 'so she knows [you]'re there', 'show that [we] are here', 'tell ... Shay, I['m] coming', 'the kid to know [I] can'. The - pole takes the obligation version ('why [they] should', 'tell them that [they] should') and the output suppresses ' should'. Probe: 'tell the manager I am' 0.70, 'knows you are there' 0.69, 'told him she had' 0.66, 'show that we are' 0.30, 'know that I care' 0.14; 'why they should' 0.11, 'that they should' 0.01, main-clause 'I am coming' 0.07.
